description: Run ONE SQL statement against the configured Snowflake account -- INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE/DDL/anything, not just reads. What the statement is actually allowed to do is decided entirely by the registered role's own server-side grants -- this verb performs no read/write classification or permission check of its own (vendor RBAC is the control plane, operator ruling 2026-08-09 + Amendment 1). Single-statement is enforced natively by the Snowflake driver, not by this plugin -- no multi-statement scripts. A statement with no result set (the common INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL case) commits and returns rowcount inline. A statement that DOES produce a result set (e.g. a RETURNING clause, where the target object supports one) routes through the same always-TSV export path as run_query: rows are never returned inline, at any size, so output_tsv_path is then required -- its absence rolls the whole statement back rather than silently discarding the returned rows while still committing the write. Returns immediately with a job_id and status 'queued' (D0.3 deferred-completion shape) -- the dispatch returning is NOT the same as the job finishing.
embedding_description: Write to the operator's Snowflake data warehouse -- INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, or DDL, whatever the connected role's own grants permit. Dispatches asynchronously, returning a job_id while the statement commits in the background. A result-producing statement lands its rows in a workspace TSV; otherwise the rowcount comes back. The one verb that changes warehouse data, not just reads it.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dispatch envelope: job_id (string) and status ('queued'). This is NOT the statement's outcome -- that arrives separately when the job completes and is delivered as its own message: either {rowcount, has_result_set: false} for a plain write, or {rowcount, has_result_set: true, path, columns, row_count, truncated} when the statement produced a result set.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This call only confirms the job was queued -- do not present job_id/status as confirmation the write happened. Acknowledge the request is in flight; the outcome lands in a follow-up message when the job completes. Once delivered: for a plain write, confirm the rowcount affected. For a result-producing statement, confirm the write AND name the TSV path/row_count/columns like run_query's export (data_sensitivity 0.5 -- never inline the file's contents). If the job instead reports an error, do not imply the write partially happened -- a failed run_statement job did not commit.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Run a SQL statement against the configured Snowflake account; the registered role's own server-side grants decide what it's allowed to do.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: snowflake.invalid_params: missing sql, output_tsv_path's parent directory does not exist, the statement produced a result set but no output_tsv_path was supplied, or acknowledge_default_limit_override/row_limit were not given together / row_limit exceeded the 1000 hard cap. snowflake.export_path_refused: output_tsv_path is not absolute, not a .tsv, or not contained under any operator-configured export_allowed_roots entry. snowflake.permission_denied: the registered role's own grants do not permit this statement -- this is the server's own access decision, not a plugin refusal. snowflake.auth_failed: the key-pair JWT was rejected. snowflake.warehouse_suspended: the configured warehouse is suspended. snowflake.timeout: the statement exceeded the statement timeout. snowflake.api_error: a SQL syntax, multi-statement, or other warehouse error.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: snowflake.invalid_params naming a result-set/missing-path mismatch: either add output_tsv_path or drop the clause that produces a result set. snowflake.invalid_params with a missing-parent message: create the parent directory first. snowflake.export_path_refused: pass an ABSOLUTE path ending in .tsv under a configured workspace root. snowflake.permission_denied: ask the operator to grant the registered role the needed privilege -- this plugin cannot and will not work around a server-side grant decision. snowflake.api_error naming a multi-statement failure: submit exactly one statement per call. snowflake.warehouse_suspended: ask the operator to resume the warehouse. snowflake.timeout: narrow the statement's scope. snowflake.auth_failed: ask the operator to check the connecting user's key.
